explanation: Reverse all characters, then reverse each maximal run of non-space characters. Word spellings are restored while word order, space-run order, and leading/trailing spaces are reversed.
timeComplexity: O(n). One full reversal and reversals of disjoint word runs touch each character a constant number of times.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space inside the callable, which reverses the supplied mutable character buffer in place. The wrapper creates an O(n) buffer/string representation for observation. Mutable native callers supply the buffer; immutable-string variants allocate a character copy and output.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/reverse_words.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Reversing the entire character array reverses the order of all word and space runs, but also reverses each word’s characters. Reversing each non-space run afterward restores its spelling without changing the run order or any spaces. Thus word order and intervening space-run order are reversed exactly as required.
walkthrough: For "red  fox blue ", reversing all characters gives " eulb xof  der". Reversing each non-space run yields " blue fox  red". The original trailing space becomes leading, and the double-space run remains doubled.
edgeCases: Only literal spaces separate words in this contract.
Repeated spaces are preserved rather than collapsed.
Leading and trailing space runs exchange positions.
Empty strings and strings consisting only of spaces remain valid.
Character positions in this implementation are UTF-8 bytes, not user-perceived grapheme clusters.
